Commentary.Commentary: What's next on the menu? A pretty one-sided affair in Edgbaston to kick off the World Cup, but the party has just started as Saturday, 13th June brings a triple delight. The day starts with Scotland Women taking on Ireland Women, followed by a delicious clash between Australia Women and South Africa Women. Both games will be played at the famous Old Trafford, Manchester. The action then shifts to Southampton for an exciting Group B clash as West Indies Women go up against New Zealand Women at The Rose Bowl to conclude the day. It all starts with the first ball of the first game, which is scheduled to be bowled at 9.30 am GMT, followed by non-stop cricketing action. But you can join us in advance for all the exciting pre-match buzz and buildup. Until then, take care, cheers!

England set the marker - Indeed, the hosts have made a strong statement with a resounding win over Sri Lanka. They bag two points and will head down south to prepare for their next assignment which will be against their neighbours, Ireland Women. That game will be played at The Rose Bowl. As far as Sri Lanka Women are concerned, they have some serious soul-searching to do and will aim to put on a much improved performance when they face the defending champions, New Zealand, in Southampton. Both these games will be played on Tuesday, 16th June.

The victorious captain of England Women - Nat Sciver-Brunt says that they started in an amazing fashion with the bat and Danni and Amy set the tone. On her return from injury, she first jokes that Danni had her running from the first ball, but then adds that she's feeling good after having those warm-up games under her belt. She further mentions the impact of coach Charlotte Edwards and tells that they are improving game by game and is looking forward to the rest of the tournament.

The captain of Sri Lanka Women - Chamari Athapaththu admits that they didn't play their best cricket today, and they failed to step up their game. Adds that their bowlers need to improve their line and length, especially their spinners. About their batting unit, she reckons that they have to play with positivity. But their effort today was not the best, and they have to perform better in the upcoming matches. Regarding their next game against New Zealand, she says that it's a tough game, but they need to execute their plan better in that match, and he hopes that they will bounce back from this result.
... Time to hear it from the captains ...

The English top three go bosh and a bang - England could not have asked for a better start to their World Cup campaign. Asked to bat, they were slightly cautious in the first 3 to 4 overs, but that nervous energy eased quickly as Sri Lanka missed chances in the field. Constant bowling changes and fielding errors did Sri Lanka no favours, and the opening duo took full toll. Danni Wyatt-Hodge targeted areas behind square on the off side while Jones used the crease well to find boundaries regularly as well. The opening stand finally broke in the 14th over, but it brought no relief, as skipper Nat Sciver-Brunt walked out with a see-ball, hit-ball approach and provided the late acceleration. Danni slowed down in the final 4 overs but still got to a well-deserved hundred on her home ground, with England's top three putting Sri Lanka to the sword to post the highest total in Women's T20 World Cup history.

Hunted in a pack - If their batting performance was solid and ruthless, England turned up with the ball even more strongly. It took 13.4 overs for Sri Lanka to pick up their first wicket, while for the hosts, they wrapped up the Sri Lankan top three inside the Powerplay. And with Chamari Athapaththu dismissed cheaply, it all went down south rather quickly for the Islanders. There was a brief fight from the likes of Harshitha Samarawickrama and Nilakshika Silva but it was all for the losing cause in the end. While one might argue that this is a pretty young and inexperienced Sri Lankan side, they would have liked to give some sort of fight with the bat, having some experienced faces in that department, but that never really happened. For England, Freya Kemp starred with the ball with a sensational 4-wicket haul, whereas with others also chipping in, they just broke the back of this Sri Lankan batting unit.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - England's Danni Wyatt-Hodge deservingly receives the award for her outstanding 105 (62)*. She says that it was quite fun out there and the crowd was amazing to play in front of. On her batting, she says that it's always to get a good start in a big tournament and she enjoyed batting alongside Amy and Nat. On her celebration, she says that it was for her daughter, Daisy. Goes on to say that the pitch was excellent to bat on and their bowlers also did a fine job. Ends by saying that she's looking forward to the next game.

The hosts decimate the Islanders - Well, that's the way to start a home World Cup. There were question marks over nerves coming in, but if anything, it was Sri Lanka who looked the more anxious side, while England were ruthless from start to finish. Big smiles and hugs all round the English camp, and why not? They have put on a complete team performance to hand out a demolition job to Sri Lanka. Their net run rate gets a big boost, and they make a strong statement from Group B, one that will give them plenty of confidence heading into their next games. For Sri Lanka, it felt like they never really turned up for the game. Costly fielding lapses, errors with the ball and a chase that never got going, everything that could have gone wrong for them, did.

Hansima is caught on the crease, trying to swipe across the line, but cannot get the bat through in time. The ball raps her on the bent back leg, in front of the off stump. A very confident shout for LBW and the finger is raised. Hansima Karunaratne walks to her partner and decides not to review this one. Sri Lanka Women are 58/4, needing 162 runs from 72 balls.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.6: Charlie Dean to Hansima Karunaratne, OUT! lbw b Charlie Dean.

Commentary.Commentary: Short, around middle and leg. Hansima Karunaratne pulls it to deep square leg. Kemp runs to her right and slides to make a safe stop. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.5: Charlie Dean to Hansima Karunaratne, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Lands it full at 86.6 kph, on middle and full in length. Harshitha Samarawickrama sits across and sweeps it hard to deep square leg, straight to Danni Wyatt-Hodge for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.4: Charlie Dean to Harshitha Samarawickrama, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A touch fuller, outside off, turning it away from the southpaw. Harshitha Samarawickrama cuts it straight to the point fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.3: Charlie Dean to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched full and around off. Harshitha Samarawickrama lofts it inside out over cover. Danielle Gibson is there who tidies it up and keeps the batters down to a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.2: Charlie Dean to Harshitha Samarawickrama, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Dean starts off offering a fuller delivery with some flight, just outside off. Hansima Karunaratne flicks it to the right of short mid-wicket and gets a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Charlie Dean to Hansima Karunaratne, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Charlie Dean (1-0-6-1) is back on.

FOUR! Cleverly done. 50 up for Sri Lanka! Back of a length, outside off. Harshitha Samarawickrama plays it very late and glides it to deep third. Lauren Bell is again in action. She runs to her right from deep point, puts in a slide but is unable to stop it. Four runs. 13 runs from Gibson's first.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Danielle Gibson to Harshitha Samarawickrama, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length delivery, outside off, Hansima Karunaratne pats it to deep point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Danielle Gibson to Hansima Karunaratne, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! A solo appeal from the keeper for caught behind, but the umpire gives it a wide. Back of a length, angling down the leg side. Hansima Karunaratne tries to pull it but misses to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Danielle Gibson to Hansima Karunaratne, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Put away! Short of a length, angled on the bodyline. Hansima Karunaratne waits for the ball to arrive and pulls it uppishly behind square on the leg side. Lauren Bell charges to her right and tries to haul the ball back in but fails to do so as it stays out of her reach and rolls into the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Danielle Gibson to Hansima Karunaratne, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a nagging length, around the thigh pad of the batter, Harshitha Samarawickrama pulls it late to deep fine leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Danielle Gibson to Harshitha Samarawickrama, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nips in a shade on a fuller length, on middle. Hansima Karunaratne tucks it to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Danielle Gibson to Hansima Karunaratne, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Danielle Gibson scoots over the wicket and bowls on a good length, angling away from the left-hander. Harshitha Samarawickrama looks to cut it through point, but gets a thick outside edge, before the ball rolls to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Danielle Gibson to Harshitha Samarawickrama, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Danielle Gibson comes in to bowl after the Powerplay.

Superb fielding once again! Very full and outside off. Hansima Karunaratne gets on the front foot and splits the backward point and cover-point gap. Lauren Bell sprints all the way to the deep and dives to flick the ball in before the ropes. The batters cross for the second run. After 6 overs, Sri Lanka Women are 39/3.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Linsey Smith to Hansima Karunaratne, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Slow and short, angling in, around the off stump. Hansima Karunaratne punches it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Linsey Smith to Hansima Karunaratne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! A third wicket for England Women inside the Powerplay, and with that, the players will take a breather. England Women are in complete control of this game right now, and Sri Lanka Women will need nothing short of a miracle to get a win from this position. However, there are plenty of overs left and a big stand through the middle overs could make things interesting. For now, Hansima Karunaratne walks out to bat at number 5.

OUT! SHARP CATCH! That's the difference so far between these two teams. England have been spotless in the field, unlike their counterparts who were extremely sloppy. On a length, around middle and leg. Dulani goes down on one knee and unleashes a hard sweep, but fails to keep it down and the ball flies straight and flat to Freya Kemp at square leg. She gets low, gets her palms in the right spot and the ball sticks like glue. England are right on top. Sri Lanka Women are struggling very badly. They are 37/3, needing 183 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Freya Kemp b Linsey Smith
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Linsey Smith to Imesha Dulani, OUT! c Freya Kemp b Linsey Smith.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, just managed to get some gloves on it. Short again, pitching it outside off and turning in toward the off pole. Imesha Dulani once again looks to reverse sweep it, but fails to get the connection and the ball hits her gloves.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Linsey Smith to Imesha Dulani, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and drifting in on off, Dulani spanks it on the bounce to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Linsey Smith to Imesha Dulani, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and well outside off, Imesha Dulani looks to reverse sweep it, but fails to get the connection.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Linsey Smith to Imesha Dulani, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! A lot quicker this time around, outside off on a length, hurries Harshitha as she attempts to steer it past point, but misses to connect. Gets beaten on the outside edge by a kitten-whisker.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Sophie Ecclestone to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, nearly played on! Spins in from off, on a fuller length. Harshitha Samarawickrama is stuck halfway and tries to put her bat on the ball, but gets an inside edge and the ball rolls past the leg stump to short fine leg. Beauty of a delivery from Ecclestone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Sophie Ecclestone to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! A confidence-building shot! Full and quick, on off, Harshitha Samarawickrama picks the length, charges down the track and smashes it between cover and mid off for boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Sophie Ecclestone to Harshitha Samarawickrama, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Spins in from outside off, on a fuller length. Harshitha Samarawickrama tries to sweep, but the ball bounces a bit and takes the top edge. Runs through short fine leg and is chased by Lauren Bell for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Sophie Ecclestone to Harshitha Samarawickrama, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Dropped short and outside off. Harshitha Samarawickrama misses to cut it away to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Sophie Ecclestone to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and drifting on the pads. Imesha Dulani shuffles far outside off and laps it fine to the deep fine leg region. The ball slows in the outfield and Heather Knight manages to chase it down from the inner ring. Three runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Sophie Ecclestone to Imesha Dulani, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Sophie Ecclestone comes into the attack, replacing Lauren Bell.

Sharp off-break, full and on off, Harshitha Samarawickrama deliberately opens the bat face to run it behind to deep third. Sophie Ecclestone from deep point runs a long way to her right to cut it off before the ropes. Two taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Charlie Dean to Harshitha Samarawickrama, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nice timing! Half volley around middle and leg, 85.5 kph. Samarawickrama shimmies across to get to the pitch of the ball and creams it through the gap between extra cover and mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Charlie Dean to Harshitha Samarawickrama, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Very full and outside off, Harshitha Samarawickrama carves it to cover, but cannot split the gap.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Charlie Dean to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on off, Harshitha Samarawickrama drives it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Charlie Dean to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Right on cue, Charlie Dean delivers. That brings Harshitha Samarawickrama to the crease.

OUT! In the air taken spectacularly! ​​Danni Wyatt-Hodge cannot do anything wrong in this game. She is having a day to remember. Dean tosses it up nicely, full and on the stumps, around off. Chamari Athapaththu goes for a premeditated sweep shot, but gets a big top edge. The ball gets ballooned towards square leg and Danni Wyatt-Hodge runs over her right shoulder, sees the ball like a hawk and takes a fine diving catch. This is a body blow to Sri Lanka as Chamari Athapaththu departs cheaply. Sri Lanka Women are 22/2, needing 198 runs more.
Commentary.Howout: c Danni Wyatt-Hodge b Charlie Dean
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Charlie Dean to Chamari Athapaththu, OUT! c Danni Wyatt-Hodge b Charlie Dean.

Commentary.Commentary: Charlie Dean seems a better match-up against Chamari Athapaththu than Linsey Smith.
Dean starts with a full ball, from around the stump. Chamari Athapaththu punches it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Charlie Dean to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Attacks the stumps, on a slightly fuller length. Imesha Dulani bunts it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Lauren Bell to Imesha Dulani, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: In and around off, full in length, Imesha pushes it gently to short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Lauren Bell to Imesha Dulani, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Good-looking shot! Short and outside off. Imesha Dulani climbs on the ball by hopping. Makes full use of the width and crunches it through the cover gap for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Lauren Bell to Imesha Dulani, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Wayward from Bell, on a good length, far down leg. Imesha Dulani shuffles to play the scoop shot, but does not lay her bat on the ball. A good diving stop by Jones to her left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Lauren Bell to Imesha Dulani, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off, Chamari Athapaththu taps it through point for an easy single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Lauren Bell to Chamari Athapaththu, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a back of a length, aimed at the pads. Imesha Dulani tries to nudge it to the leg side, but gets beaten and the ball is deflected off the thigh pad to deep fine leg for a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Lauren Bell to Imesha Dulani, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Sprays it way down leg, on a fuller length. Imesha Dulani walks inside the line and misses to flick. Wide called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Lauren Bell to Imesha Dulani, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Not the best of reviews from Sri Lanka Women. Imesha Dulani now walks out to bat.

OUT! LBW! As usual, it is Bell to provide the first wicket for the hosts. She lands it on a fractionally fuller length and aims the stumps. Vishmi Gunarathne walks forward and looks to whip it across, but her head falls over and she plays all around it getting struck on the front pad. A confident appeal for LBW and up goes the finger instantly. Looks dead-straight but Vishmi Gunarathne has taken the review after having a chat with her captain. UltraEdge presents a flat line. Ball Tracking shows the impact is in line and the ball is projected to crash into the middle stump. Three reds and Vishmi Gunarathne is gone. Sri Lanka lose the review, and their first wicket. They are 14/1, chasing 220.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Lauren Bell to Vishmi Gunarathne, OUT! lbw b Lauren Bell.

Commentary.Commentary: Too full, on middle, Vishmi carves it over the bowler. It rolls down the ground and is mopped up by Capsey to her left from long off. One run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Linsey Smith to Vishmi Gunarathne, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and sliding in on off, Vishmi steps out and takes it on the full, hitting it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Linsey Smith to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full again, on off, Chamari lofts it over the bowler and the ball once again plugs in the deep. The long off fielder cuts it off to her left. One taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Linsey Smith to Chamari Athapaththu, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drops it full and on off, Chamari Athapaththu clears the front leg and hoists it over mid on, but unluckily for Chamari, the ball lands and just plugs into the damp outfield at long on for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Linsey Smith to Chamari Athapaththu, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Looped up on middle. Chamari takes it on the full and shovels it to the mid on fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Linsey Smith to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Low full toss on off, from around the stump. Vishmi Gunarathne mistimes it and forces it to mid off for a tight single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Linsey Smith to Vishmi Gunarathne, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Decent start for the Lankans with the bat. Linsey Smith, the left-arm spinner to operate from the other end.

FOUR LEG BYES! Just straying down leg on a fuller length. Chamari Athapaththu misses the flick on the inswinging ball and the ball grazes her front pad and beats the diving Amy Jones to her right. The ball just stays out of her reach and races away to the fence behind. 9 runs off the first over of the chase.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Lauren Bell to Chamari Athapaththu, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, moving away, on off. Vishmi Gunarathne walks out of the crease to negate the swing. Tries to pull but misses and the ball also beats Amy Jones, who dives to her right. Rolls through her gloves towards the left of deep third for a bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Lauren Bell to Vishmi Gunarathne, Bye.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Finds the gap to get the chase underway for Sri Lanka! Much fuller but wide outside off. The ball keeps moving away from the batter and Vishmi Gunarathne leans on, throws her bat at it and threads it through backward point and short third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Lauren Bell to Vishmi Gunarathne, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, curving away from the batter. Vishmi gets a bit squared up and blocks it to short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Lauren Bell to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: At 109.4 kph, this is full and around off, swinging away. Vishmi Gunarathne pushes it gently to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Lauren Bell to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bell is on the money and almost creates a chance! A hint of away swing from leg to middle, full in length. Vishmi Gunarathne looks to flick it to the leg side but the excessive movement ekes a leading edge but the ball lands in front of the mid off fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Lauren Bell to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.
